analysis: Examined head SSDBlockStreamingTests.swift; the only change is the new test readExactlyAssemblesShortReads (lines 259-283). It exercises SSDBlockStore.readExactly with a beforeRead charge callback, asserting that short reads are reassembled into the full span, that the result has startIndex 0, and that the charge sequence matches. The expected sequence is [count, 0] for a full read and [count, 0, 0] when the file grows mid-read. This is test-only code, writes inside a temp fixture root and adds no production attack surface. The test does reveal production semantics that integration should verify in SSDBlockStore.swift, which is not supplied here and is relevant to T-041(c) DBK3 integrity and read budgeting. First, readExactly charges the full requested count up front, then makes zero-count calls on later loop iterations. Second, readExactly loops on a short read instead of failing immediately at EOF; the test only grows the file on the third callback. Integration should confirm that readExactly still fails closed on true EOF and cannot spin indefinitely on a stalled or truncated file. Third, combined with the cursor and identity tracking (onAuthenticatedFile, SSDAuthenticatedFileChange at lines 212-230), integration should confirm that file growth or change during a read is still detected before plaintext reaches the consumeChunk sink. AES-GCM per-chunk authentication still rejects altered bytes. Existing tests for header bounds, authentication ordering and requireEOF are unchanged. No regression identified from this unit alone.
